oast_dryer.text: Up there's the drying floor: slats of wood with horsehair cloth over, and the hops spread a foot deep. Below, the fire, burning day and night for weeks in September.
The drier slept here in the oast and turned the hops with a big wooden scuppet. Too hot and they scorch, too cool and they go mouldy. Get it right and the whole valley smells of beer.
Some oasts burned sulphur on the fire too, to keep the hops a nice green colour. You can still smell it on old beams, on a warm day.

oast_presser.text: The dried hops go into long sacks called pockets, pressed in tight. A full pocket weighs about as much as two grown men and smells better than either.
